citation.quote: During the 1914–1918 war, Kropotkin had sided with the western empires against the central powers, in a declaration known as the "Manifesto of the Sixteen."

title: Assassination of Jean Jaures
summary: French Republican and Social Democratic leader Jean Jaures was assassinated on the eve of the First World War.

citation.quote: Jean Jaures (1859–1914), Republican and Social Democratic leader, journalist and historian, assassinated on the eve of the First World War.

title: Pestaña becomes CNT national secretary
summary: Angel Pestaña moved from the secretariat of the Metalworkers' Union to the CNT national secretaryship in 1914.

citation.quote: Angel Pestana (1886–1937), watch-maker, moved from the secretariat of the Metalworkers' Union to the CNT national secretaryship in 1914

title: Malatesta ignites the Red Week in Ancona
summary: Malatesta lit the fuse of the 'Red Week' after the forces of law and order massacred unarmed demonstrators; the people took over the city, the trade unions called a nationwide general strike, and the army intervened.

citation.quote: In June 1914, he lit the fuse of the "Red Week." Disturbances erupted after the forces of law and order massacred unarmed demonstrators. The people took over the city. The trade unions called a nationwide general strike.

title: Voline arrested in France, flees to the United States
summary: His anti-war activities led to his arrest in 1915; threatened with internment in a concentration camp, Voline sailed for the United States as a coaltrimmer aboard a steamship.

citation.quote: As a member since 1913 of the International Anti-War Action Committee, his activities led to his being placed under arrest in 1915. Threatened with internment in a concentration camp, Voline successfully sailed aboard a steamship, as a coaltrimmer, for the United States.

title: Anti-war manifesto signed by thirty-five libertarians
summary: A manifesto opposing the First World War was issued and signed by thirty-five well-known libertarians of various nationalities, including Errico Malatesta, Alexander Schapiro, Alexander Berkman, Emma Goldman, and Domela Nieuwenhuis.

citation.chapter: MALATESTA, THE ANARCHIST INTERNATIONAL, AND WAR
citation.quote: The manifesto below uas issued on February 15, 1915. It was signed by thirty-five well-known libertarians of various nationalities–among them Errico Malatesta, Alexander Schapiro, Alexander Berkman, Emma Goldman, Domela Nieuwenhuis, etc.

title: Manifesto of the Sixteen endorses the war
summary: Kropotkin, Tcherkessoff, Jean Grave, Charles Malato, Christian Cornelisse, Paul Reclus and other anarchists issued a declaration approving the war, carried in France by La Bataille Syndicaliste; it became known as the "Manifesto of the Sixteen" though it had only fifteen signatories.

citation.chapter: MALATESTA, THE ANARCHIST INTERNATIONAL, AND WAR
citation.quote: On a contrary note, in the spring of 1916, some other anarchists, including Kropotkin, Tcherkessoff, Jean Grave, Charles Malato, Christian Cornelisse, Paul Reclus (son of Elisee), etc., issued a declaration approving tlie war. In France, it was carried by La Bataille Syndicaliste, a news-sheet suspected of being subsidized by the French government. This declaration became famous as the "Manifesto of the Sixteen," although, in fact, it had only fifteen signatories.

title: Anarchist-communists protest the Manifesto of the Sixteen
summary: Anarchist-communists issued a protest against the pro-war Manifesto of the Sixteen, denouncing its propaganda as nationalistic and reactionary, and declaring its signatories enemies of the working class.

citation.chapter: MALATESTA, THE ANARCHIST INTERNATIONAL, AND WAR
citation.quote: In May 1916, it elicited a protest from anarchist-communists, which concluded with these words:

title: Voline returns to revolutionary Russia with Golos Truda
summary: The editors of the Russian anarcho-syndicalist weekly Golos Truda, including Voline, arrived in revolutionary Russia intent on transferring the publication to Saint Petersburg.

citation.quote: In 1917, its editors–and with them, Voline–arrived in revolutionary Russia, intent upon transferring the weekly to Saint Petersburg.

title: Two contrary notions of social revolution clash in Russia
summary: At the time of the Russian overthrow in 1917, two opposing visions of social revolution—the Bolshevik statist-centralist approach and the anarchist federalist approach—came into direct conflict.

citation.quote: Such also were the two contrary notions of social revolution at the time of the Russian overthrow in 1917

title: Mass uprising of 1917
summary: Sailors and workers were the grassroots architects of the 1917 mass uprising, the revolution whose authors Guerin contrasts with the later crushing of Kronstadt.

citation.quote: But how could these sailors and workers–once the grassroots architects of the mass uprising of 1917 who were about to perish under the gunfire of the Red officer cadets and Mongolian troops have retained the historian's objectivity and sung the praises of their executioners?

title: Kronstadt sailors defend Berkman from extradition
summary: The Kronstadt sailors staunchly defended Alexander Berkman when he was in danger of being extradited to California.

citation.quote: The presence of Sasha, whom the Kronstadt sailors had staunchly defended when he was in danger of being extradited to California in 1917, and myself, whom the sailors knew by reputation, would have added weight to the resolution, they said.

title: Aaron Baron returns to Russia
summary: After escaping to the United States, Aaron Baron returned to Russia in 1917 and became joint editor with Voline of the Kharkov newspaper Nabat.

citation.quote: escaped to the United States, returning to Russia in 1917: joint editor with Voline of the Kharkov newspaper Nabat

title: Lenin publishes The State and Revolution
summary: Lenin's The State and Revolution appeared in 1917.

citation.quote: Lenin, *The State and Revolution,* 1917.

title: Plekhanov breaks with Lenin over Bolshevik seizure of power
summary: Russian populist-turned-Marxist Georgi Plekhanov, mentor and collaborator of Lenin, broke with him in 1917 in order to condemn the Bolshevik seizure of power.

citation.quote: Georgi Plekhanov (1856–1918), a Russian populist turned marxist in exile: pioneered marxism in Russia: mentor and collaborator of Lenin, before breaking with him in order to condemn the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917.

title: February Revolution realizes the soviets
summary: The February 1917 revolution overthrew tsarism and promptly realized the idea of workers' and peasants' councils (Soviets) that had first been advocated before the 1905 revolution.

citation.chapter: HOW COMMUNISM SHOULD NOT BE INTRODUCED
citation.quote: The idea of Soviets, that is, of workers' and peasants' councils, first advocated prior to the attempted revolution of 1905 and promptly realized by the February 1917 revolution, once tsarism had been overthrown, the idea of such councils controlling the country's political and economic life, is a grand idea.

title: Kropotkin returns to Russia
summary: After nearly thirty years in England, Kropotkin returned to Russia in the spring of 1917, under the Kerensky government.

citation.quote: ...for the next thirty years, he was to dwell in England, only to return to Russia in the spring of 1917, under Kerensky.

title: Kronstadt sailors support March 1917 uprising
summary: The Kronstadt sailors came out in support of workers during the March 1917 uprising in Russia.

citation.quote: Keeping faith with their revolutionary traditions and with solidarity among toilers, as so loyally demonstrated during the 1905 revolution and later during the uprisings in March and October of 1917, they again came out in support of the harassed workers of Petrograd.

title: Trotsky sails from New York for Russia
summary: Leon Trotsky and his family sailed from New York, bound for Russia, departing in the wake of the February Revolution.

citation.quote: Trotsky and his family sailed from New York, bound for Russia, on March 17, 1917.

title: Voline meets Trotsky in New York printworks
summary: While both were preparing to return to Russia, Voline encountered Trotsky at a New York printworks; Trotsky was editing the left-marxist daily Novy Mir, and Voline was editing the anarcho-syndicalist weekly Golos Truda.

citation.quote: In April 1917, I happened to be in New York with Trotsky, in a printworks which worked primarily for various left-wing Russian bodies. At the time, he was in charge of a left marxist daily paper, Novy Mir.

title: Revolutionary strike erupts; Durruti joins the CNT
summary: The revolutionary strike of August 1917 erupted; in León it ended with workers sacked and leaders persecuted. Durruti, drawn to the CNT's participation, joined the union for life.

citation.quote: It was then that the revolutionary strike of August 1917 erupted; in Leon, it ended with workers being sacked and their leaders persecuted. The Leon branch of the National Confederation of Labor (CNT) also participated in the strike.

title: Kropotkin returns to Russia after the October revolution
summary: Kropotkin returned to the land of his birth following the October revolution of 1917, after which he produced important writings as the 'anarchist prince.'

citation.quote: in order not to split up Kropotkin's various writings, u e have opted to skip a number of years and turn now to the important writings of the "anarchist prince,"' from the time that he returned to the land of his birth after the October revolution of 1917.

title: Russian Revolution enters terrain of social revolution
summary: From October 1917, according to Voline, the Russian revolution entered new territory as a great social revolution, proceeding along a novel and original route.

citation.quote: From October 1917 on, the Russian revolution entered quite new terrain: that of the great social revolution. Thus, it proceeded along a very specific route, virgin territory.

title: Kronstadt sailors support October Revolution
summary: The Kronstadt sailors came out in support of the October 1917 uprising, becoming staunch supporters of the Bolsheviks.

citation.quote: Keeping faith with their revolutionary traditions and with solidarity among toilers, as so loyally demonstrated during the 1905 revolution and later during the uprisings in March and October of 1917, they again came out in support of the harassed workers of Petrograd.

title: Central Rada becomes parliament of Ukrainian republic
summary: From November 1917 on, the Central Rada functioned as a sort of parliament of the new "Ukrainian democratic republic."

citation.quote: From November 1917 on, the Central Rada was a sort of parliament of the new "Ukrainian democratic republic."

title: Anarchist influence alarms the Bolsheviks
summary: By the end of 1918, the influence of the anarchist idea among the laboring masses had grown to such an extent that the Bolsheviks, intolerant of opposition, became seriously worried.

citation.quote: By the end of 1918, this influence had become such that the Bolsheviks, who would brook no criticism, let alone contradiction or opposition, were seriously worried.

title: Bolshevik State broadly established
summary: The Bolshevik State—the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics—was broadly established during 1918–1921, claiming to be a 'proletarian' or 'worker and peasant' State exercising the dictatorship of the proletariat.

citation.quote: The Bolshevik State, broadly established in 1918–1921, has been in existence for twenty years.

title: Makhnovitsi rise against bourgeois and occupying authorities
summary: Peasants and workers known as the Makhnovitsi rose up against the brutality of bourgeois, German, Hungarian and Austrian authorities and the hetman of the Ukraine.

citation.quote: The MAKHNOVITSI are peasants and workers who rose up as long ago as 1918 against the brutality of the bourgeois, German, Hungarian and Austrian authorities and against that of the hetman of the Ukraine.

title: Publication of Mehring's biography of Karl Marx
summary: Franz Mehring's Karl Marx, Geschichte seines Lebens was published.

citation.quote: Franz Mehring (1846–1919), Karl Marx, Geschichte seines Lebens 1918

title: Noske becomes governor of Kiel
summary: Right-wing Social Democrat Gustav Noske became governor of Kiel in 1918.

citation.quote: Gustav Noske (1868–1946), right-wing Social Democrat, governor of Kiel in 1918, joined the counterrevolutionary council of people's commissars at the start of 1919

title: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk opens Ukraine to Austro-Germans
summary: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, agreed between the Bolsheviks and the German imperial government at the beginning of 1918, opened the gates of the Ukraine to the Austro-Germans, who set up a reactionary government headed by hetman Skoropadsky.

citation.quote: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, agreed between the Bolsheviks and the German imperial government at the beginning of 1918, had opened the gates of the Ukraine to the Austro-Germans.

title: Central Powers' defeat forces German withdrawal from Ukraine
summary: The defeat suffered by the Central empires towards the end of 1918 forced the withdrawal of German and Austrian troops from the Ukraine, while Skoropadsky fled and was replaced by a Directory headed by Petliura.

citation.quote: But the defeat suffered by the Central empires towards the end of 1918 forced the withdrawal of German and Austrian troops from the Ukraine, while Skoropadsky took to his heels. He was replaced by a "Directory," headed by a former member of the Rada, the bourgeois separatist, Petliura.

title: Bolsheviks raid Moscow anarchist federation
summary: On the night of April 12, 1918, Bolshevik police and military troops ransacked the premises of the Moscow federation of anarchist groups, a private hotel situated in the Malaia Dmitrovka.

citation.quote: On a specious pretext, the Bolshevik authorities, on the night ofApril 12, 1918, had had their police and military troops ransack the premises of the Moscow federation of anarchist groups, a private hotel situated in the Malaia Dmitrovka.

title: Makhno travels to Moscow and meets Sverdlov and Lenin
summary: Nestor Makhno traveled to Moscow to consult with anarchist militants about revolutionary work among the Ukrainian peasantry, taking the opportunity to meet with Yakov Sverdlov and Lenin at the Kremlin.

citation.quote: In June 1918, Makhno went to Moscow for consultations with some anarchist militants regarding methods and approaches to the revolutionary libertarian work needing to be done among the Ukrainian peasantry. He availed of the occasion to present himself at the Kremlin and meet with Yakov Mikhailovitch Sverdlov, the then secretary of the Bolshevik Party's Central Committee, and then with Lenin himself.

title: Lenin grants Makhno an audience
summary: Lenin granted Nestor Makhno an audience in June 1918, making Makhno not quite unknown to the Bolsheviks.

citation.quote: Makhno was not quite unknown to the Bolshe­ viks, for Lenin, as we have seen, granted him an audience in June 1918.

title: Armistice prompts German-Austrian withdrawal from Ukraine
summary: The November 11, 1918 armistice led to the withdrawal of the German-Austrian armies of occupation from Ukraine, giving Makhno an opportunity to accumulate weapons.

citation.quote: The armistice on November 11, 1918 led to a withdrawal of the German-Austrian armies of occupation, as well as offering Makhno a unique opportunity to accumulate weapons reserves and stock-pile.

title: Ukrainian anarchist conference in Kursk
summary: Voline was one of the prime movers behind a Ukrainian anarchist conference in Kursk, where he was commissioned to draft the resolutions and a unifying declaration, leading him to articulate the idea of an "anarchist synthesis".

citation.quote: A little later, he joined the newspaper Nabat ("The Tocsin") and became one of the prime movers behind a Ukrainian anarchist conference in Kursk on November 18, 1918.

title: First Congress of the Anarchist Organizations of the Ukraine (Nabat)
summary: The Nabat anarchist federation held its first congress in Ukraine, resolving to unite anarchist strands and to participate actively in the Makhnovist insurgent movement against reactionary forces.

citation.quote: ORGANIZATIONS OF THE UKRAINE (NABAT), NOVEMBER 18, 1918

title: Kropotkin's letter to Georg Brandes
summary: Kropotkin wrote a letter to his friend Georg Brandes describing the isolated life he and his family led in their provincial Russian town and offering his assessment of the situation in Russia.

citation.quote: LETTER TO GEORG BRANDES (1919)

title: Malatesta returns to Italy from London
summary: By the end of 1919, Malatesta was able to leave London to return to Italy, where he was greeted by enthusiastic crowds and became a leading light of the Unione Sindacalista Italiana (USI).

citation.quote: By the end of 1919, he was able to leave London to return to Italy, where he was greeted by enthusiastic crowds.

title: Bolshevik war against the anarchist movement
summary: From 1919 until the end of 1921, the Bolsheviks waged a savage struggle against the spread of anarchist ideas, at least as long and as bitter as their struggle against the reaction.

citation.quote: From 1919 on, and up until the end of 1921, they were to wage a very savage struggle against this idea's onward march: a struggle at least as long and as bitter as the struggle against the reaction had been.

title: Civil war between Bolsheviks and anarchists in Ukraine
summary: In Ukraine, the unequal struggle between Bolshevik authorities and anarchist-inspired popular movements escalated into full-scale civil war that lasted more than two years, forcing the Bolsheviks to mobilize all their resources.

citation.quote: So, the strife between the two approaches to social revolution and, by the same token, between the Bolshevik authorities and certain movements of the toiling masses occupied a very important place in the events of the years between 1919 and 1921.

title: Nabat secretariat scattered; member captured by White Guards
summary: Denikin's advance scattered the Nabat secretariat; one member was captured by the White Guards in the autumn of 1919, two others joined the Makhnovitsi, and a fourth (Voline) was arrested in Moscow.

citation.chapter: THIRD CONGRESS OF THE ANARCHIST ORGANIZATIONS OF THE UKRAINE
citation.quote: In the end, the Nabat's own secretariat was scattered and its members put to flight. One of them was captured by the White Guards in the autumn of 1919, two others joined the ranks of the MAKHNOVITSI and fought with them against Denikin, while the fourth (Voline was arrested in Moscow.

title: Anarchist insurgents eradicate Denikin's counter-revolution
summary: According to Piotr Arshinov, the chronicler of the Makhnovshchina, the anarchist insurgents were chiefly responsible for eradicating Denikin's counter-revolution in the autumn of 1919.

citation.quote: "The honor of having eradicated Denikin's counter-revolution in the autumn of 1919 belongs chiefly to the anarchist insurgents," writes Piotr Arshinov, the chronicler of the Makhnovshchina.

title: Makhnovists drive Denikin back toward the Sea of Azov
summary: After a series of skirmishes in early 1919, the Makhnovist insurgents pushed Denikin's troops back toward the Sea of Azov, capturing around a hundred wagon-loads of wheat which were sent to famished workers in Moscow and Petrograd.

citation.quote: At the beginning of 1919, after a series of skirmishes, the Makhnovist insurgents drove Denikin's troops back in the direction of the Sea of Azov and captured around one hundred wagon-loads of wheat from them.

title: Goldman deported from United States to Russia
summary: Emma Goldman was deported from the United States to Russia, arriving in Petrograd where she would witness the Kronstadt revolt.

citation.quote: Deported from the United States to Russia in 1919, Goldman happened to be in Petrograd just when the Bolsheviks made up their minds to crush the Kronstadt revolt.

title: Death of Franz Mehring
summary: Franz Mehring, biographer of Marx, died.

citation.quote: Franz Mehring (1846–1919), Karl Marx, Geschichte seines Lebens 1918

title: Goldman deported from the United States to Soviet Russia
summary: In 1919, with the anti-anarchist witch-hunt at its height, Emma Goldman was deported from the United States to Soviet Russia.

citation.quote: In 1919, with the anti-anarchist witch-hunt at its height, she was deported from the United States to Soviet Russia.

title: Berkman deported to Soviet Russia
summary: Alexander Berkman was arrested and deported along with Emma Goldman in 1919 to Soviet Russia.

citation.quote: He was arrested and deported along with her in 1919 to Soviet Russia.

title: Scheidemann becomes German Social Democrat chancellor
summary: Philip Scheidemann served as German Social Democrat chancellor in 1919.

citation.quote: Philip Schedidemann (1864–1935), German Social Democrat chancellor in 1919.

title: Noske joins counterrevolutionary council of people's commissars
summary: Gustav Noske joined the counterrevolutionary council of people's commissars at the start of 1919, then became Army minister organizing repression of post-war revolutionary movements.

citation.quote: joined the counterrevolutionary council of people's commissars at the start of 1919, then went on to become Army minister, organizing the repression of the post-war revolutionary movements.

title: Kneller fires on Elysee Palace
summary: French activist Michel Kneller fired revolver shots at the Elysee Palace in 1919 in protest at the blockade on soviet Russia.

citation.quote: Michel Kneller, a French activist who, in 1919, fired revolver shots at the Elysee Palace in

title: Cottin attempts to assassinate Clemenceau
summary: The young anarchist Louis-Émile Cottin attempted the life of French premier Georges Clemenceau in 1919; sentenced to death, his punishment was commuted to ten years' imprisonment.

citation.quote: Louios-Émile Cottin (1896–1936), anarchist: while still a youth, he attempted the life of premier Georges Clemenceau in 1919. Sentenced to death, his punishment was commuted to ten years' imprisonment.

title: First regional congress of Gulyai-Polye
summary: The first regional congress of the Makhnovist movement took place spontaneously at the first insurgent camp in Greater Mikhailovka, consisting of delegates from districts adjacent to the front, in order to coordinate the front and introduce uniformity of organization across the region.

citation.quote: The first regional congress took place on January 23 this year in the first insurgent camp in Greater Mikhailovka. It consisted of delegates from the districts adjacent to the front.

title: Second regional congress at Gulyai-Polye
summary: The second regional congress was summoned to Gulyai-Polye by a steering committee of five elected by the first congress; it established the Gulyai-Polye regional military revolutionary council with one delegate per district, totalling thirty-two members from the Ekaterinoslav and Tauride governments.

citation.quote: The regional military revolutionary council was set up i n accordance with the resolution from the second congress held in Gulyai-Polye on February 12th this year.

title: Second Nabat congress denounces the soviets
summary: A second Nabat congress declared participants categorically opposed to all participation in the soviets, which had become purely political bodies organized on authoritarian, centralist and statist foundations.

citation.quote: A second *Nabat* congress was held in March–April 1919. Participants declared themselves to be "categorically and irreversibly opposed to all participation in the soviets, which have become purely political bodies, organized on authoritarian, centralist and Statist foundations."

title: Second congress of the Nabat confederation
summary: The second congress of the full members of the Nabat confederation was held in March–April 1919.

citation.chapter: THIRD CONGRESS OF THE ANARCHIST ORGANIZATIONS OF THE UKRAINE
citation.quote: The third congress of the full members of the Nabat confederation took place in particularly difficult circumstances. After the second congress (in March–April of 1919), a further congress had been scheduled for August that year, but it was unable to proceed because of the sweeping offensive unleashed in june by the White general, Denikin.

title: Makhnovist and Red Armies cooperate against Denikin
summary: Faced with the gravity of the interventionist threat, Makhno's forces and the Red Army came to an accommodation, acting in concert against Denikin in March 1919.

citation.quote: However, the two armies twice came to another accommodation, when the gravity of the interventionist threat required that they act in concert–action which came, first, against Denikin in March 1919 and then, in the summer of 1920, when Wrangel's White troops threatened before Makhno put them to flight.

title: Makhnovist insurgent army incorporated into the Red Army
summary: The Bolshevik fighters' first encounter with Makhno took place under auspices of goodwill in March 1919, and Makhno was invited to join the Red Army with his detachments to jointly defeat Denikin while retaining his army's internal order and black flags.

citation.quote: The Bolshevik fighters' first encounter with Makhno took place under the same auspices of goodwill and praise (in March 1919). Makhno was immediately invited to join the Red Army along with all his detachments, with an eye to joining forces in order to defeat Denikin.

title: Bavarian Councils republic in Munich
summary: Erich Mühsam was involved in the government of the Bavarian Councils republic, which survived for only six days in Munich (April 7–13, 1919), alongside Gustav Landauer.

citation.quote: involved in the government of the Bavarian Councils republic, which survived for only six days in Munich (April 7–13, 1919) along with Gustav Landauer (1870–1919), an anarchist writer brutally done to death

title: Third Gulyai-Polye regional congress and Dybenko's denunciation
summary: The third regional congress proceeded in Gulyai-Polye with representatives from 72 cantons; Dybenko sent a telegram declaring the congress counter-revolutionary and outlawing its organizers, prompting a vigorous protest from the assembled delegates.

citation.quote: "Comrade" Dybenko declared the congress scheduled for Gulyai-Polye on April 10, 1919 counter-revolutionary and outlawed its organizers, against whom, he claims, the severest repressive measures must be enforced.

title: Kropotkin's letter to the workers of Western Europe
summary: Kropotkin writes from Dmitrov, Moscow Guberniya, to the workers of Western Europe warning against foreign military intervention in Russia and against the Bolsheviks' one-party state communism.

citation.chapter: HOW COMMUNISM SHOULD NOT BE INTRODUCED
citation.quote: DMITROV, MOSCOW GUBERNIYA, APRIL 28, 1919

title: Whites launch second campaign against Makhnovists
summary: The White forces under Denikin opened their second campaign on a vast scale that even the Makhnovists had not anticipated, while Bolsheviks remained preoccupied with their plan against the Makhnovshchina.

citation.quote: With all the more commitment, the Whites laid the groundwork for their second campaign, which opened in May 1919 on a huge scale which even the Makhnovists had not anticipated.

title: Military revolutionary council decides to convene extraordinary congress
summary: At its sitting on May 30, the executive committee of the Gulyai-Polye military revolutionary council resolved to summon an extraordinary congress in Gulyai-Polye on June 15 to address the White onslaught and the situation of soviet power.

citation.quote: At its sitting on May 30, the executive committee of the military revolutionary council, after scrutiny of the impact upon the front of the onslaught of White gangs, and consideration of the overall political and economic situation of soviet power, came to the conclusion that only the toiling masses themselves, and not individuals or parties, can devise a solution to this.

title: Summons issued to Fourth Extraordinary Congress
summary: The Executive Committee of the Military Revolutionary Council issued from Gulyai-Polye a summons (Telegram No. 416) to the Fourth Extraordinary Congress of peasant, worker, and partisan delegates.

citation.quote: Signed: The Executive Committee of the Military Revolutionary Council. Dated: Gulyai-Polye, May 31, 1919.

title: Denikin launches sweeping offensive against the Ukraine
summary: A planned August Nabat congress was prevented when the White general Denikin unleashed a sweeping offensive in June 1919, smashing liaison between anarchist organizations.

citation.chapter: THIRD CONGRESS OF THE ANARCHIST ORGANIZATIONS OF THE UKRAINE
citation.quote: After the second congress (in March–April of 1919), a further congress had been scheduled for August that year, but it was unable to proceed because of the sweeping offensive unleashed in june by the White general, Denikin.

title: Trotsky issues Order No. 1824 banning the congress
summary: From Kharkov, Trotsky issued Order No. 1824 of the Military Revolutionary Council of the Republic, forbidding the planned Makhnovist congress, declaring participation an act of high treason, and ordering the arrest of delegates.

citation.quote: ORDER NO. I 824 OF THE MILITARY REVOLUTIONARY COUNCIL OF THE REPUBLIC, JUNE4, 1919, KHARKOV

title: Cossacks occupy Gulyai-Polye
summary: A veritable avalanche of Don and Kuban Cossacks descended upon Gulyai-Polye and occupied it on June 6, 1919, after defeating the hastily raised peasant regiment near Sviatodukhovka.

citation.quote: Whereupon a veritable avalanche of Cossacks descended upon Gulyai-Polye, occupying it on June 6, 1919.

title: Bolsheviks send Makhno an armored train
summary: On June 7, the Bolsheviks sent Makhno an armored train and urged him to hold out to the bitter end, promising further reinforcements while concealing Trotsky's order to seize him.

citation.quote: On June 7, they sent Makhno an armored train, urging him to hold out to the bitter end and promising that further reinforcements would follow.

title: Makhno resigns command in letter to Soviet leadership
summary: From Gaitchur Station, Makhno sent a written explanation to Voroshilov, Trotsky, Lenin, and Kamenev, formally resigning his command in response to Order No. 1824 and the Bolshevik campaign against the insurgent movement.

citation.quote: Signed: Father Makhno Gaitchur Station, June 9, 1919.

title: Libertarian Youth in Paris adopts name Ni Dieu ni Maître
summary: Le Libertaire reported on June 25, 1919 that the Libertarian Youth founded in Paris had adopted the name Ni Dieu ni Maître.

citation.quote: During the 1914–1918 war, Sebastien Faure revived the catch-phrase and, once peace had returned, the Libertarian Youth founded in Paris adopted the name **Ni Dieu ni Maître**, as *Le Libertaire* reported on June 25, 1919.

title: Voline joins Makhno's Ukrainian anarchist guerrilla
summary: As the Bolshevik authorities began suppressing the free press and arresting anarchists, Voline managed to link up with the headquarters of Nestor Makhno's Ukrainian anarchist guerrilla.

citation.quote: It was at that point, July 1919, that Voline managed to link up with the headquarters of the Ukrainian anarchist guerrilla, Nestor Makhno.

title: Malatesta's prophetic letter to Luigi Fabbri
summary: Errico Malatesta writes from London to Luigi Fabbri, warning that the Bolshevik 'dictatorship of the proletariat' has become the dictatorship of one party's leaders and predicting that, like Robespierre's dictatorship preparing the way for Napoleon, Lenin and Trotsky's governmental structures will be used to crush the revolution.

citation.chapter: A PROPHETIC LETTER TO LUIGI FABBRI1
citation.quote: London, July 30, 1919

title: Makhnovist congress in Alexandrovsk adopts General Theses
summary: Voline chaired a congress of the Makhnovist insurgent movement held in Alexandrovsk, which adopted the General Theses spelling out the doctrine of "free soviets".

citation.quote: He chaired a congress of the insurgent movement, the one held in October 1919, in Alexandrovsk. It saw the adoption *of General Theses,* which spelled out the doctrine of "free soviets"

title: Regional peasants' and workers' congress at Alexandrovsk
summary: A regional peasants' and workers' congress was held in Alexandrovsk with over 200 delegates (180 peasants and several dozen workers), examining military issues against Denikin and civilian life, with proceedings lasting more than a week and featuring reports by the anarchist Voline.

citation.quote: A regional peasants' and workers' congress was held in Alexandrovsk on October 20, 1919. Upwards of two hundred delegates took part, 180 of them peasants and two or three dozen workers.

title: Voline arrested by Bolsheviks in Makhnovist region
summary: Gravely wounded, Voline was arrested by Bolshevik military authorities in the Makhnovist region. Trotsky telegraphed orders to 'Shoot out of hand,' but Voline escaped execution by fortuitous circumstances.

citation.quote: In December 1919, gravely wounded, I was arrested by the Bolshevik military authorities in the Makhnovist region. Deeming me a militant "of some standing," the authorities notified Trotsky of my arrest by means of a special telegram asking his view of how I should be handled.

title: CNT provisionally affiliates to the Third International
summary: At its Madrid congress, the CNT declared itself a defender of Bakunin's principles in the First International and resolved to affiliate provisionally to the Third International, pending a true workers' international congress to be held in Spain.

citation.quote: The National Confederation of Labor declares itself a staunch defender of the principles upheld by Bakunin in the First International. It declares further that it affiliates provisionally to the Third International on account of its predominantly revolutionary character, pending the holding of the International Congress in Spain, which must establish the foundations which are to govern the true workers' International.

title: Pestana charged to travel to Moscow
summary: The CNT congress tasked Angel Pestana with traveling to Russia to attend the second congress of the Third International and convey the confederal congress's decisions.

citation.quote: (...) Angel Pestana was charged to travel to Russia in order to attend the second congress of the Third International and communicate the decisions taken by the confederal congress.

title: December 1919 Congress of the CNT
summary: The CNT held its congress in December 1919, a key gathering of Spanish anarcho-syndicalism.

citation.quote: THE DECEMBER 1919 CONGRESS OF THE CNT

title: CNT national congress held in Madrid
summary: The CNT's national congress convened in Madrid and debated trade union amalgamation, a national federations-of-industry structure, and a libertarian communist statement of principles, which was carried unanimously.

citation.quote: The CNT's national congress was held in Madrid from December 10 to 18, 1919. It dealt with three major issues: amalgamation of the Spanish proletariat's trade union centrals (defeated by 325,955 votes to 169,125, with 10,192 abstentions), a new organizational format based upon national federations of industry (rejected by 651,472 votes to 14,008) and a statement of libertarian communist principles (carried unanimously by acclamation).

title: Makhno routs Wrangel's White troops
summary: In the summer of 1920, the Makhnovists again cooperated with the Red Army when Wrangel's White troops threatened, and Makhno put them to flight.

citation.quote: ...action which came, first, against Denikin in March 1919 and then, in the summer of 1920, when Wrangel's White troops threatened before Makhno put them to flight.

title: Durruti returns to Spain
summary: The breath of revolution sweeping Europe prompted Durruti's return to Spain at the beginning of 1920, where he found Manuel Buenacasa in San Sebastian and joined Los Justicieros.

citation.quote: The breath of revolution sweeping Europe prompted his return to Spain at the beginning of 1920. In San Sebastian, he found Manuel Buenacasa, who was the general secretary of the CNT Construction Union there.

title: Brupbacher joins Communist Party
summary: Fritz Brupbacher became a member of the Communist Party in 1920 (he was expelled at the end of 1932).

citation.quote: he was a member of the Communist Party from 1920 up until he was expelled from that at the end of 1932.

title: Execution of Alexis Koltchak
summary: White Russian general Alexis Koltchak was defeated and shot by the Bolsheviks.

citation.quote: Alexis Koltchak (1874–1920), White Russian general defeated and shot by the Bolsheviks

title: Millerand serves as president of the Republic
summary: Alexandre Millerand served as president of the French Republic from 1920 to 1924.

citation.quote: Alexandre Millerand (1859–1943), reformist socialist who became a minister in 1899 and president of the Republic from 1920 to 1924.

title: Funeral of Émile Pouget
summary: Émile Pouget was buried in the village of Lozère (Palaiseau), with Pierre Monatte, Maurice Chambelland, Daniel Guérin and others following his pauper's hearse.

citation.quote: In 1920, in the village of Lozere (Palaiseau), a pauper's hearse, followed by Pierre Monatte, Maurice Chambelland and a few others, myself (Daniel Guerin) among them, bore Émile Pouget to his final resting place.

title: Admiral Koltchak shot
summary: Admiral Alexis Koltchak, who had waged war on revolutionary Russia in Siberia from 1918 to 1919, was shot in 1920.

citation.quote: Admiral Alexis Koltchak (1874-1920) waged war on revolutionary Russia in Siberia (1918–1919) and was shot in 1920

title: Victor Chernov quits Russia
summary: Victor Chernov, a leader of the Social Revolutionary Party and post-February 1917 government minister, was forced to quit Russia in 1920.

citation.quote: Victor Chernov (1876–1952), one of the leaders of the Social Revolutionary Party, was a government minister after the revolution of February 1917 and had to quit Russia in 1920.

title: Borghi travels to Russia, meets Lenin
summary: Armando Borghi, general secretary of the Italian Syndicalist Union, traveled to Russia in 1920 and met Lenin there.

citation.quote: Armando Borghi (1882–1968), general secretary of the Italian Syndicalist Union, an anarcho­ syndicalist labor organization, traveled to Russia in 1920 and had met Lenin there

title: Manifesto of the Insurgent Army of the Ukraine issued
summary: The Revolutionary Councils of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (makhnovitsi) publish a manifesto annulling Denikinist ordinances, transferring estates to peasants and factories to workers, and calling for free workers' and peasants' councils.

citation.chapter: MANIFESTO OF THE INSURGENT ARMY OF THE UKRAINE
citation.quote: **ARMY OF THE UKRAINE** **(JANUARY 1, 1920)**

title: Corriere della Sera hails Malatesta as a leading figure
summary: The Corriere della Sera portrayed Malatesta as 'one of the greatest figures in Italian life'; his newspaper Umanità Nova had a print-run of 50,000 copies.

citation.quote: The *Corriere* della *Sera* of January 20, 1920 portrayed him as "one of the greatest figures in Italian life."

title: Makhnovist program/manifesto issued
summary: The Makhnovitsi issued a program and manifesto outlining their aims: overthrow of monarchist, social democratic, and Bolshevik-Communist governments, in favor of free worker and peasant soviets.

citation.quote: PROGRAM/MANIFESTO OF APRIL 1920

title: Makhnovist Program/Manifesto drafted
summary: The Program/Manifesto of April 1920 was drafted by the cultural and educational branch of the Makhnovist Insurgent Army.

citation.quote: Drafted by the cultural and educational branch of the Makhnovist Insurgent Army.

title: Second Congress of the Communist International
summary: The Second Congress of the Communist International convened in June 1920, attended by international delegations including Angel Pestaña.

citation.quote: THE SECOND CONGRESS OF THE COMMUNIST INTERNATIONAL (JUNE 1920)

title: Second Congress of the Communist International opens in Moscow
summary: The Third International's second congress opened in Moscow. Zinoviev moved that the Spanish CNT be accepted as a member of the Third International's Executive Committee, which was agreed.

citation.quote: The Third International's second congress opened on 28 June 1920 in its headquarters in Moscow. Straight off, Zinoviev moved that the Spanish Confederation be accepted as a member of the Third International's Executive Committee, which was agreed.

title: Third Congress of the Nabat Anarchist Federation
summary: The third congress of the Ukrainian Anarchists' Nabat Federation met September 3–8, 1920 under the surveillance of the Cheka, passing resolutions rejecting the 'transitional period' and the 'dictatorship of labor.'

citation.chapter: THIRD CONGRESS OF THE ANARCHIST ORGANIZATIONS OF THE UKRAINE
citation.quote: Passed at the Ukrainian Anarchists' Nabat Federation Congress, meeting from September 3 to 8, 1920.

title: Pestana leaves Russia after Comintern congress
summary: Angel Pestana departed Russia following the second congress, after a brief exchange with Italian Syndicalist Union delegate Armando Borghi, both disheartened by the experience and aware of the plan for a Communist-controlled Red International of Labor Unions.

citation.quote: Pestana left Russia on September 6, 1920, after a short exchange of impressions with Armando Borghi' (...) the delegate from the Italian Syndicalist Union (USI), who returned to Italy disheartened by this unfortunate experience.

title: Voline freed by Cheka under Bolshevik-Makhno agreement
summary: After six months as a member of Makhno's military council, Voline had been arrested by the 14th Red Army and held by the Cheka in Moscow; he regained his freedom in October 1920 under a military agreement between the Bolshevik government and Makhno.

citation.quote: But he was arrested by the 14th Red Army, taken to Moscow and placed in the care of the political police (Cheka). Not until October 1920 would he regain his freedom under a military agreement between the Bolshevik government and Makhno.

title: Cheka ambush kills Makhno's Crimean officers
summary: At the end of November 1920, Bolshevik authorities laid an ambush, inviting officers of Makhno's Crimean army to a military council where they were arrested by the Cheka and shot or disarmed.

citation.quote: At the end of November 1920, the 13olshevik authorities had no hesitation in laying an ambush. The officers of Makhno's Crimean army were invited to participate in a military council. Whereupon they were promptly arrested by the political police, the Cheka, and shot out of hand, or stripped of their weapons.

title: Aaron and Fanya Baron arrested by Cheka
summary: Aaron Baron and his companion Fanya were arrested by the Cheka in November 1920 and kept in prisons and concentration camps until 1938.

citation.quote: arrested by the Cheka along with his companion Fanya in November 1920, he was kept in prisons and concentration camps until 1938

title: Vilkens' last visit to Kropotkin
summary: Vilkens visits the seventy-eight-year-old Kropotkin, who discusses the Russian Revolution and criticizes Bolshevik methods for making communism hateful to the people.

citation.quote: VILKENS' LAST VISIT TO KROPOTKIN' (DECEMBER, 1920)

title: Voline re-arrested in Kharkov on eve of anarchist congress
summary: After traveling to Kharkov to prepare an anarchist congress scheduled for December 25 with the Nabat Confederation, Voline was arrested by the Bolsheviks on the eve of the congress along with other anarchists who had served with Makhno.

citation.quote: Whereupon he traveled to Kharkov where, in concert with the *Nabat* Confederation, he laid the preparations for an anarchist congress scheduled for December 25. On the eve of the congress, the Bolsheviks had Voline arrested once again, along with any anarchists who had served with Makhno.

title: Kronstadt revolt crushed
summary: The Kronstadt revolt was the culmination of the accumulated errors of the Bolshevik authorities between 1918 and 1921, ending in the sailors and workers being killed by Red officer cadets and Mongolian troops.

citation.quote: The accumulated errors of the Bolshevik authorities between 1918 and 1921, of which Kronstadt was to be the culmination, in no way diminished the revolutionary convictions or genius of the authors of the October Revolution.

title: Assassination of Eduardo Dato
summary: Spanish prime minister Eduardo Dato was assassinated; Durruti later visited imprisoned comrades and the journalist Mauro Bajatierra, held as an accessory in the case.

citation.quote: Durruti traveled to Madrid with the dual mission of attending the conference and speaking to the comrades imprisoned following the assassination of Eduardo Dato' in 1921.

title: Kronstadt revolt
summary: Emma Goldman stayed in Soviet Russia up until the Kronstadt revolt in 1921, then returned to Europe and America.

citation.quote: She stayed there up until the Kronstadt revolt (1921). Then she returned to Europe and America

title: Rocker publishes The Bankruptcy of Russian State Communism
summary: German anarchist historian Rudolf Rocker authored The Bankruptcy of Russian State Communism (in German) in 1921.

citation.quote: Rudolf Rocker (1873–1958), German anarchist historian and philosopher who died in the United States. Author, notably of *The Bankruptcy of Russian State Communism* (in German), 1921.

title: Founding of the Communist Party of Great Britain
summary: Tom Mann took part in the founding of the Communist Party of Great Britain in 1921.

citation.quote: joined the American revolutionary syndicalist Industrial Workers of the World (IWW): took part in the founding of the Communist Party of Great Britain in 1921.

title: Lozovsky becomes chairman of the Profintern
summary: Salomon Lozovsky became chairman of the Red International of Labor Unions (Profintern) from 1921 until 1937.

citation.quote: Chairman of the Red International of Labor Unions (Profintern) from 1921 to 1937.

title: Le Libertaire publishes Vilkens' last visit to Kropotkin
summary: An account of Vilkens' last visit to Kropotkin appeared in the newspaper Le Libertaire on January 28, 1921.

citation.quote: Taken from the newspaper Le Libertaire, of January 28, 1921.

title: Kropotkin's funeral procession in Moscow
summary: Following Kropotkin's death, his body was brought to Moscow where masses of mourners — unarmed soldiers, sailors, students, peasants and anarchists with red and black banners — followed the cortege for two hours to Devishy cemetery, in the largest demonstration since October.

citation.quote: The homage paid to the respect and affection inspired by Peter Kropotkin turned Moscow into one enormous demonstration. From the moment the body arrived in the capital and was delivered to the trade union headquarters, through the two days when the corpse was on display in the marble hall, there was such a procession of people as had not been witnessed since the events of October.

title: Anarchists temporarily released to attend Kropotkin's funeral
summary: After the funeral commission threatened to publicly denounce the soviets, Kamenev agreed to free imprisoned anarchists; only seven from the Cheka prison were released as pall-bearers, while none from Butyrky prison were freed.

citation.quote: The funeral was delayed for one hour. The huge masses of mourners shivered in the cruel cold of Moscow, waiting for the imprisoned disciples of the great deceased to arrive on the streets. In the end, arrive they did, but there were only seven of them in the entire Cheka prison.

title: Death of Peter Kropotkin in Dmitrov
summary: Peter Kropotkin died of pneumonia at four o'clock in the morning at his villa in Dmitrov, with Emma Goldman arriving an hour too late to tend him.

citation.quote: Alas! We were too late! Peter had breathed his last an hour earlier. He had died at four o' clock on the morning of February 8, 1921.

title: Lenin announces New Economic Policy at Tenth Party Congress
summary: Three days after the fall of Kronstadt, at the Communist Party's tenth congress in Moscow, Lenin unexpectedly announced the New Economic Policy (NEP), reversing three years of policy on free trade and labor markets.

citation.quote: The true implications of this "liquidation" of Kronstadt were disclosed by Lenin himself three days after the nightmare. At the Communist Party' s tenth congress, held in Moscow, while the siege of Kronstadt was in progress, Lenin unexpectedly switched from his inspired paeans to communism to an equally fervent paean to the New Economic Policy.

title: Kronstadt uprising
summary: The Kronstadt uprising of March 1921 — the rebellion of Baltic sailors and workers against Bolshevik rule, suppressed by the Red Army.

citation.quote: This newspaper had been launched well before the uprising of March 1921.

title: Kronstadt mass rally passes resolution supporting strikers
summary: At a street rally attended by 16,000 sailors, Red Army soldiers and workers, the First and Second Squadron of the Baltic Fleet passed resolutions in support of the Petrograd strikers, with only three dissenting voices.

citation.quote: The example set by these crews was taken up by the First and Second Squadron of the Baltic Fleet stationed in Kronstadt. At a street rally on March 1, attended by 16,000 sailors, Red Army soldiers and workers from Kronstadt, similar resolutions were passed unanimously, except for three dissenting voices.

title: Baltic Fleet Squadrons pass Kronstadt Resolution
summary: The General Assembly of the 1st and 2nd Squadrons of the Baltic Fleet adopted a fifteen-point resolution calling for new soviet elections by secret ballot, freedom of speech and press, release of socialist prisoners, and other reforms.

citation.quote: RESOLUTION PASSED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE 1ST AND 2ND SQUADRONS OF THE BALTIC FLEET, HELD IN KRONSTADT (March 1, 1921)

title: Mass meeting in Kronstadt endorses crews' resolution
summary: A great meeting in Kronstadt unanimously endorsed a resolution from the 1st and 2nd squadrons' crews, demanding fresh elections to the soviets.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: This determination on the part of all toilers, Red soldiers and sailors was demonstrated plainly at the great meeting in our town on March 1st. The meeting unanimously endorsed a resolution from the 1st and 2nd squadrons' crews.

title: Provisional Revolutionary Committee established in Kronstadt
summary: Delegates from the fleet, garrison, and workers met in the Education College and established the Provisional Revolutionary Committee, with headquarters aboard the Petropavlovsk.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: the delegates from all of the fleet organizations, the garrison and the workers met on March 2 in the Education College. That meeting was to draw up the basis for fresh elections and thereby embark upon positive, peaceable work, the task of overhauling the soviet system.

title: First issue of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The first issue (No. 1) of the Kronstadt Izvestia appeared, carrying the Provisional Revolutionary Committee's address to the population of the fortress and town of Kronstadt.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: [NO. 1, MARCH 3, 1921] TO THE POPULATION OF THE FORTRESS AND TOWN OF KRONSTADT

title: Delegate meeting expands the Provisional Revolutionary Committee
summary: At 6:00 PM in the Garrison Club, twenty-two delegates from military units and trade unions met and elected ten new members to expand the Provisional Revolutionary Committee.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: A DELEGATE MEETING–Yesterday, March 4th, at 6:00 P.M., there was a meeting in the Garrison Club of delegates from the military units and trade unions, summoned in order to expand the Provisional Revolutionary Committee through the election of further members, and to hear reports on developments in progress.

title: Issue No. 2 of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The second issue of the Kronstadt Izvestia appeared with the Provisional Revolutionary Committee's address warning of impending Communist attack.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING

title: Goldman and Berkman submit appeal against Kronstadt assault
summary: Berkman, Goldman and two others submitted a written appeal to the Petrograd Soviet and Zinoviev urging a peaceful, fraternal settlement of the Kronstadt conflict via a five-person commission including two anarchists.

citation.quote: Petrograd, March 5, 1921. Alexander Berkman, Emma Goldman, 'and two additional signatures'

title: Issue No. 3 of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The third issue of Kronstadt Izvestia appeared under the headline 'Victory or Death,' reporting on the delegate meeting of March 4.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING

title: Issue No. 4 of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The fourth issue of Kronstadt Izvestia carried an editorial, a broadcast appeal to all workers, and a letter from a rank-and-file Communist.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: [NO. 4, MARCH 6, 192I]

title: Issue No. 5 of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The fifth issue carried an editorial denouncing Trotsky's threats and reported wireless exchanges with Petrograd about sending delegates.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: [NO. 5, MARCH 7, 192I]

title: Bolshevik artillery opens fire on Kronstadt
summary: At 6:45 PM, Communist batteries in Sestroretsk and Lissy Noss were the first to open fire on the Kronstadt forts, with Krasnaya Gorka subsequently joining and being answered by the battleship Sebastopol. Two Red soldiers wounded.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: At 6:45 P.M., the Communist batteries in Sestroretsk and Lissy Noss became the first to open fire on the Kronstadt forts. The forts accepted the challenge and quickly reduced those batteries to silence. Whereupon it was Krasnaya Gorka that opened fire. To a worthy reply from the battle-ship 'Sebastopol.'

title: Issue No. 6 of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The sixth issue announced the first bombardment of Kronstadt and addressed the working women of the world on International Women's Day.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING
citation.quote: [NO. 6, MARCH 8, 192I] FIRST COMMUNIQUE

title: Eduardo Dato assassinated
summary: Ultra-reactionary Spanish premier Eduardo Dato was assassinated by CNT metalworkers on March 8, 1921, in Madrid, in reprisal for the White terror in Barcelona.

citation.quote: Eduardo Dato, ultra-reactionary Spanish premier, assassinated by CNT metalworkers on March 8. 1921, in Madrid, in reprisal for the White terror enforced in Barcelona with Dato's consent by governor Martinez Anido.

title: Issue No. 7 of Kronstadt Izvestia published
summary: The seventh issue carried the address 'Listen, Trotsky!' denouncing the Communist authorities for concealing the rebels' wireless messages from the population.

citation.chapter: THE OFFICIAL JOURNAL OF THE KRONSTADT UPRISING

title: Bombardment of Kronstadt ends
summary: After ten days and nights of non-stop bombardment, the assault on Kronstadt ceased abruptly on the morning of March 17 as the town fell to Bolshevik forces, with tens of thousands killed.

citation.quote: The bombardment of Kronstadt continued non-stop for ten days and ten nights, ceasing abruptly on the morning of March 17. The silence which shrouded Petrograd was more daunting than the endless cannonades of the previous night.

title: Kronstadt liquidation marked on Paris Commune anniversary
summary: On the 50th anniversary of the Paris Commune of 1871, the Communists marched through Petrograd singing the Internationale to mark the crushing of Kronstadt.

citation.quote: March 18: the anniversary of the Paris Commune of 1871, crushed after two months by Thiers and Gallifet, the butchers of thirty thousand Communards! Re-enacted in Kronstadt on March 18, 1921.

title: Foundation congress of the Red International of Labor Unions
summary: Leval participated as a CNT delegate in the foundation congress of the Red International of Labor Unions, held in the wake of the third Communist International congress in Moscow.

citation.quote: Gaston Leval, born the son of a Communard in 1895 and himself a French anarcho-syndicalist militant, was a participant in the foundation congress of the Red International of Labor Unions in June–August 1921 in the wake of the third congress of the Communist International, as a delegate from the Spanish CNT.

title: Makhno flees to Romania
summary: Outnumbered and outgunned, Makhno was obliged to give up the struggle and fled into Romania in August 1921, before moving on to Paris.

citation.quote: In the end, thwarted by forces far outnumbering him and better equipped, Makhno was obliged to give up. He managed to flee into Rumania in August 1921, before moving on to Paris, where he was to die much later, in July 1935, ailing and impoverished.

title: Fanny Baron shot by the Bolsheviks
summary: Fanny Baron was shot by the Bolsheviks in September 1921.

citation.quote: Fanny Baron was shot by the Bolsheviks in September 1921.

title: Berkman leaves Russia for Germany
summary: In December 1921, after the crushing of the Kronstadt revolt and the execution of Fanny Baron, Alexander Berkman left Russia for Germany and then France.

citation.quote: In December 1921, after the crushing of the Kronstadt revolt and the execution of Fanny Baron, he left Russia for Germany and then on to France.

title: Publication of Berkman's The Bolshevik Myth
summary: Alexander Berkman's The Bolshevik Myth was published.

citation.quote: and The Bolshevik Myth (1922).

title: Schapiro leaves for Berlin after Bolshevik crackdown
summary: The Bolshevik crackdown on anarchists forced Alexander M. Schapiro to leave for Berlin in 1922, where he became driving force behind the exiled Russian anarchist group.

citation.quote: The Bolshevik crack-down on the anarchists forced him to leave for Berlin in 1922, there to be the driving force behind the exiled Russian anarchist group.

title: Maximoff forced out of Russia, emigrates to Berlin
summary: Anarcho-syndicalist Grigori Petrovitch Maximoff was forced to quit his native Russia in 1922, going first to Berlin where he was active in the International Workers' Association.

citation.quote: He was forced to quit his native land in 1922 for Berlin, where he was active in the International Workers' Association, and then for Paris: he then emigrated to the United States, in 1925...

title: Berkman publishes The Bolshevik Myth
summary: Alexander Berkman published the English-language pamphlet The Bolshevik Myth (covering 1920-1921) in 1922.

citation.quote: The Bolshevik Myth (1920-1921) was to be the title of a pamphlet published in English by

title: Sanz organizes the Los Solidarios group
summary: Construction worker Ricardo Sanz organized the anarchist action group 'Los Solidarios' in 1922.

citation.quote: Ricardo Sanz (born 1900), construction worker, organized the anarchist action group "Los Solidarios" in 1922

title: Durruti moves to Barcelona
summary: Amid escalating violence and the freeing of imprisoned CNT militants in Zaragoza, Durruti decided in January 1922 to go and live in Barcelona.

citation.quote: In this climate, Durruti, a close friend of Ascaso and of Torres Escartin,1 made up his mind in January 1922 to go and live in Barcelona.

title: Labor Alliance general strike smashed by fascists
summary: The antifascist Labor Alliance, which Malatesta had attempted to forge with political parties and trade unions, called a general strike in July 1922, but it was smashed by the rising power of the fascist blackshirts.

citation.quote: He transferred his newspaper to Rome and attempted to conclude an antifascist "Labor Alliance" with the political parties and trade unions: in July 1922, the Alliance called a general strike, but the attempt was smashed by the rising power of the fascist blackshirts.

title: First congress of the CGTU at Saint-Etienne
summary: Henri Sirolle reported on his experiences as a delegate in Moscow in 1921 at the first congress of the CGTU in Saint-Etienne in July 1922.

citation.quote: at the first congress of the CCTU in Saint-Etienne in July 1922, reporting on his experiences as a delegate in Moscow in 1921, he told how, at an audience with Lenin, the latter had shown him a few files on anarchists...

title: Lehning's article on Marxism and Anarchism published in Berlin
summary: Arthur Lehning's article 'Marxism and Anarchism in the Russian Revolution' was published in the review Die Internationale in Berlin.

citation.quote: Arthur Lehning, "Marxism and Anarchism in the Russian Revolution," in the review Die International, Berlin, 1923.

title: Monatte joins the French Communist Party
summary: Pierre Monatte joined the French Communist Party in 1923 and became editor of the social affairs page in L'Humanité.

citation.quote: In 1923 he joined the French Communist Party and became editor of the social affairs page in L'humanite.

title: Assassination of Salvador Seguí
summary: Salvador Seguí, a famous CNT militant, public speaker and organizer, was murdered in Barcelona.

citation.quote: On March 10, 1923, Salvador Segui,' a very famous militant, great public speaker and superb organizer, was murdered.

title: Salvador Segui murdered
summary: Catalan trade union organizer and great libertarian leader Salvador Segui was murdered by the hired killers of Catalonia's governor Martinez Anido on March 10, 1923.

citation.quote: Salvador Segui (1896–1923), Catalan and brilliant public speaker, trade union organizer and cultural promoter: protagonist of the SINDICATO ÚNICO (single union) instead of the trades union. Murdered by the hired killers of Catalonia's governor, Martinez Anido, on March 10, 1923.

title: Anarchist conference in Madrid
summary: Zaragoza's Libre Acuerdo anarchist group summoned an anarchist conference in Madrid; Durruti attended and was arrested as it concluded, but freed days later.

citation.quote: Around this time, militant anarchism was looking to launch a more homogeneous organization, and Zaragoza's LIIIRE AcUERDo anarchist group summoned an anarchist conference for the month of April in Madrid.

title: Execution of Cardinal Soldevila in Zaragoza
summary: Amid nation-wide upheavals between May and June 1923, Cardinal Soldevila was executed in Zaragoza; Francisco Ascaso and Torres Escartín were indicted, with only Ascaso escaping.

citation.quote: There were tremendous nation-wide upheavals between May and June 1923. In Zaragoza, Cardinal Soldevila was executed. In the wake of that execution, Francisco Ascaso and Torres Escartin were indicted.

title: Durruti and Ascaso procure arms in Eibar
summary: Durruti and Ascaso set out from Bilbao to purchase a sizable consignment of weapons from an arms plant in Eibar for the planned insurrection.

citation.quote: in June 1923, Durruti and Ascaso set out from Bilbao to purchase a sizable consignment. They procured some from an arms plant in Eibar, through the good offices of an engineer.

title: Primo de Rivera's coup d'état
summary: General Primo de Rivera mounted his coup d'état in September 1923, preventing the landing of the arms shipment intended for the planned insurrection.

citation.quote: the weapons only reached Barcelona after General Primo de Rivera had mounted his coup d'é*tat* in September 1923.

title: Malatesta publishes Pensiero e Volontà
summary: Malatesta brought out a bimonthly review, Pensiero e Volontà, in 1924; though frequently censored, it survived into 1926 and carried articles of consummate maturity.

citation.quote: Even so, he managed to bring out a bimonthly review, *Pensiero e Volontà,* in 1924: though frequently censored, it survived into 1926.

title: Durruti and Ascaso leave for Cuba
summary: Towards the end of 1924, Durruti and Ascaso left for Cuba, beginning a campaign of agitation in favor of the Spanish revolutionary movement.

citation.quote: Towards the end of 1924, Durruti and Ascaso left for Cuba (...) There they embarked upon a campaign of agitation in favor of the Spanish revolutionary movement.

title: Mühsam amnestied
summary: After being sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment by a court martial for his role in the Bavarian Councils republic, Erich Mühsam was amnestied at the end of 1924.

citation.quote: Mühsam was sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment by a court martial, then amnestied at the end of 1924.

title: Gregorio Sobreviela murdered
summary: Anarchist trade unionist Gregorio Sobreviela, wanted by police for several coups de main and attentats, was murdered in February 1924.

citation.quote: Gregorio Sobreviela, metalworker and anarchist trade unionist, wanted by police for a number of coups de main and attentats: murdered in February 1924.

title: Monatte expelled from the Communist Party
summary: Pierre Monatte was expelled from the French Communist Party in November 1924, after which he launched La Révolution Prolétarienne.

citation.quote: He was expelled from the Party in November 1924, whereupon he launched La Revolution Proletarienne, organ of the Ligue syndicaliste.

title: Maximoff emigrates to the United States
summary: Maximoff emigrated to the United States in 1925, where he published anarchist newspapers in Russian and later wrote Twenty Years of Terror in Russia.

citation.quote: he then emigrated to the United States, in 1925, where he published anarchist newspapers in Russian and published, in English, one of the finest books on the Russian Revolution viewed from the anarchist perspective, Twenty Years of Terror in Russia (1940).

title: Malatesta placed under house arrest by fascists
summary: From the end of 1926 onwards, fascist totalitarianism reduced the aged Malatesta to silence; he lived under house arrest, which prevented him from joining the Spanish republican revolution in 1931.

citation.quote: From the end of 1926 onwards, the aged Malatesta, whom fascist totalitarianism had reduced to silence (except for a few articles which he managed to smuggle out of the country), was living under house arrest, which is what stopped him from joining the republican revolution in Spain in 1931 as he would have wished.

title: Petritchenko's testimony published in Znamya Borby
summary: Petritchenko's testimony on the Kronstadt uprising was published in the January 1926 edition of Znamya Borby.

citation.quote: Published in the January 1926 edition of Znamya Borby: taken from Ida Mett, La Commune de Cronstadt (Editions Spartacus, 1938, new edition 1948).

title: Durruti and Ascaso arrested in Paris
summary: After a clandestine return via Cherbourg, Durruti and Ascaso were arrested by French police in Paris on the formal grounds of conspiring against King Alfonso XIII.

citation.quote: They put ashore clandestinely in Cherbourg in April 1926. From there, they traveled to Paris, where they lodged in a hotel in the Rue Legendre. It was as they emerged from that hotel that they were arrested by French police one morning.

title: Attempted attack on King Alfonso XIII in France
summary: Gregorio Jover, along with Durruti and Ascaso, was involved in a would-be attack on King Alfonso XIII in France on July 14, 1926.

citation.quote: Gregorio Jover (1892–1964?), trade union organizer, libertarian activist who was involved in a would-be attack on King Alfonso XIII in France, along with Durruti and Ascaso on July 14, 1926

title: Trial of Durruti, Ascaso and Jover in Paris
summary: Durruti and Ascaso appeared before the criminal court charged with unlawful possession of weapons, rebellion and breaches of the law on aliens, declaring they had intended to seize King Alfonso XIII.

citation.quote: In October that year, they appeared before the criminal court charged with unlawful possession of weapons, rebellion and breaches of the law on aliens.

title: Death of Georg Brandes
summary: Georg Brandes, Danish literary critic, died.

citation.quote: Georg Brandes (1842–1927), renowned Danish literary critic.

title: Publication of Anarchie et organisation
summary: Malatesta's Anarchie et organisation was published in 1927, and later republished in 1967.

citation.quote: 2. *Anarchic et organisation* (1927), republished 1967.

title: Three Spanish anarchists freed in Paris
summary: Following a defense campaign led by Louis Lecoin, Ferandel and Sébastien Faure mobilizing French political, intellectual and working-class circles, Durruti, Ascaso and Jover were freed.

citation.quote: Several newspapers backed the campaign, and in July 1927, the three Spanish anarchists were freed.

title: Arshinov publishes History of the Makhnovist Movement
summary: Piotr Arshinov's book documenting the Makhnovist movement in the southern Ukraine was published, serving as a primary source for accounts of the free communes and insurgent army.

citation.quote: The texts below are taken from Piotr Arshinov's 1928 book History of the Makhnovist Movement.

title: Durruti enters Germany illegally
summary: In autumn 1928, Durruti and companions succeeded in entering Germany illegally to make contact with Rudolf Rocker and Erich Mühsam, who tried to secure them political refugee status.

citation.quote: In autumn 1928, they finally succeeded in entering Germany illegally, there to make contact with Rudolf Rocker' and Erich Mühsam, who attempted to secure political refugee status for them.

title: Andler's Nietzsche, sa vie et sa pensée, Volume IV published
summary: Charles Andler's study Nietzsche, sa vie et sa pensée, Volume IV, was published, discussing Nietzsche's affinity with Stirner.

citation.quote: "So profoundly at one with Stirner did he feel that in his day he was alraid of being perceived as his plagiarist." (Ch. Andler, Nietzsche, sa vie et sa pensee, Volume IV, 1928)

title: Maurin founds the Worker and Peasant Bloc
summary: After breaking with Moscow, Joaquin Maurin founded the Worker and Peasant Bloc in 1931.

citation.quote: Joaquin Maurin (born 1897), the founder, successively, of the Communist Federation of Catalonia, then, after his break with Moscow, of the Worker and Peasant Bloc (1931) and then of the Workers' Party of Marxist Unification-POUM, (1935...

title: Durruti and Ascaso leave Brussels for Spain
summary: After staying in Brussels with false papers and collaborating with the Comité Pro-Liberté, Durruti returned to Spain on the proclamation of the Republic.

citation.quote: They stayed in Brussels until April 13, 1931. At this point in their careers as militants, they tasted a measure of tranquillity.

title: Revolutionary demonstration in Barcelona
summary: A revolutionary show of strength was held in the Bellas Artes hall in Barcelona, followed by a demonstration of a hundred thousand people demanding freedom for prisoners and social reforms, broken up by army and Civil Guard.

citation.quote: A revolutionary show of strength on May 1, 1931 was held in the Bellas Artes hall in Barcelona. A demonstration by a hundred thousand people followed, and the demonstrators paraded through Barcelona's streets up to the Generalidad Palace

title: Paris publication of Bakunin's Confession
summary: Bakunin's 1857 Confession to the Tsar was published in Paris.

citation.quote: Extracted from Confession (1857 Letter to the Tsar), Paris, 1932.

title: Brupbacher expelled from Communist Party
summary: Fritz Brupbacher was expelled from the Communist Party at the end of 1932.

citation.quote: he was a member of the Communist Party from 1920 up until he was expelled from that at the end of 1932.

title: Durruti deported to the Canaries after Figols events
summary: Durruti was deported to Puerto Cabra on the island of Fuerteventura in the Canaries, where he spent the months between February and September 1932 after the Figols uprising.

citation.quote: He came to prominence in the events in Figols and was deported to the Canaries, to Puerto Cabra on the island of Furteventura, where he was obliged to spend the months between February and September 1932.

title: Death of Errico Malatesta
summary: Errico Malatesta died on July 22, 1932.

citation.quote: He died on July 22, 1932.

title: Casas Viejas uprising
summary: In 1933 the workers of Casas Viejas took over their village and proclaimed libertarian communism; the Civil Guards put the rebellion down with savagery.

citation.quote: In 1933, the workers of Casas Viejas had taken over their village and proclaimed libertarian communism. The Civil Guards had put this rebellion down with savagery.

title: Revolutionary uprising of January 1933
summary: Durruti was active in the revolutionary uprising of January 1933 and was imprisoned from January to August that year.

citation.quote: He was also active in the revolutionary uprising of January 1933 and was again imprisoned from January to August that year.

title: Mühsam arrested by the Nazis
summary: German revolutionary poet and anarchist Erich Mühsam was arrested by the Nazis on February 28, 1933, in the aftermath of the Reichstag fire.

citation.quote: Arrested by the Nazis on February 28, 1933, he was murdered by the S.S. in a concentration camp on the night of July 9–10, 1934

title: Durruti joins National Revolutionary Committee
summary: In December 1933, Durruti was on the National Revolutionary Committee, but was imprisoned in Burgos and Zaragoza from December 1933 to July 1934.

citation.quote: In December 1933, Durruti was on the National Revolutionary Committee, but from December 1933 to July 1934 was again sent to prison in Burgos and Zaragoza

title: Publication of Goldman's Living My Life
summary: Emma Goldman's memoirs Living My Life were published in 1934.

citation.quote: Taken from Emma Goldman, Living my Life, 1934.

title: Pestaña launches the Syndicalist Party
summary: After being expelled from the CNT as leader of the reformist 'Thirty' current, Angel Pestaña launched a Syndicalist Party in 1934, representing it in the Spanish parliament until 1936.

citation.quote: In 1934, he launched a Syndicalist Party, which he represented in the Spanish parliament up to 1936

title: Asturias strike radicalizes Largo Caballero
summary: The 1934 Asturias strike radicalized reformist socialist Francisco Largo Caballero, secretary of the UGT.

citation.quote: secretary of the General Workers' Union (UGT): radicalized during the Asturias strike in 1934

title: Mühsam murdered by the SS
summary: Erich Mühsam was murdered by the SS in a concentration camp on the night of July 9–10, 1934.

citation.quote: he was murdered by the S.S. in a concentration camp on the night of July 9–10, 1934

title: Durruti sentenced to penal servitude
summary: Durruti was sentenced to penal servitude on October 5, 1934 until mid-1935.

citation.quote: only to be sentenced to penal servitude on October 5, 1934 until mid–1935.

title: Founding of POUM
summary: Joaquin Maurin co-founded the Workers' Party of Marxist Unification (POUM) in 1935.
