title: Death of Nestor Makhno in Paris
summary: Nestor Makhno died in Paris in July 1935, ailing and impoverished, after years of exile following his flight from Ukraine.

citation.quote: He managed to flee into Rumania in August 1921, before moving on to Paris, where he was to die much later, in July 1935, ailing and impoverished.

title: Durruti jailed again, freed before February 1936 elections
summary: Durruti was jailed again in September 1935, only to be freed days ahead of the elections of February 1936.

citation.quote: He was jailed again in September 1935, only to be freed days ahead of the elections of February 1936.

title: Popular Front government invoked as parallel to 1848
summary: Proudhon's strictures against the legalistic stewards of 1848 are compared by Guérin to the members of the 1936 Popular Front government under Léon Blum.

citation.quote: And Proudhon gave a sound thrashing to those who, like the members of the Popular Front government of 1936, had but one thought in their heads: keeping within the bounds of the law.

title: Anarcho-syndicalists boost Spain's economic development
summary: Santillan recounts that in 1936 the trade union organizations gave a powerful fillip to Spain's economic development, adding fervor and effort to existing plant as a first step in raising industrial and agricultural levels.

citation.chapter: THE WRITINGS OF DIEGO ABAD DE SANTILLAN
citation.quote: In 1936, we were able to give a powerful fillip to Spain's economic development, because we added the fervor of belief and intensification of effort to the existing plant.

title: CNT debates dissolving the Antifascist Militias Committee
summary: The CNT and libertarian movement debated whether to transform the Antifascist Militias Committee of Barcelona into the Generalidad Council of Catalonia, ultimately choosing participation in state bodies over isolation.

citation.chapter: FEDERICA MONTSENY SETS THE RECORD STRAIGHT
citation.quote: Above all, one has to appreciate the contemporary context and view things, not through a thirty–year looking-glass, but bearing in mind the situation in which the CNT and the libertarian movement were placed in 1936.

title: Publication of Santillán's El Organismo económico de la Revolución
summary: Santillán's El Organismo económico de la Revolución was published.

citation.quote: Santillan, El Organismo económico de la Revolución, 1936

title: Emma Goldman visits Spain
summary: In 1936, Emma Goldman visited Spain.

citation.quote: In 1936, she visited Spain.

title: Suicide of Alexander Berkman
summary: Alexander Berkman committed suicide in Nice, in poor health.

citation.quote: In poor health, he committed suicide in Nice.

title: Santillán publishes El organismo económico de la revolución
summary: Diego Abad de Santillán published his outline of the economic organism of the revolution prior to the July 1936 Spanish Revolution.

citation.quote: Catalonia, published this outline prior to the revolution of July 1936: (this extract is from his book El organisrno economico de la revolucion, 1936).

title: Prudhommeaux launches L'Espagne antifasciste
summary: Andre Prudhommeaux published the earliest editions of L'Espagne antifasciste in 1936, followed by L'Espagne nouvelle in 1937.

citation.quote: he published the newspaper Terre libre and a collection of pamphlets under the title Cahiers de terre libre, the earliest editions of L'Espagne antifasciste (1936) and later L'Espagne nouvelle (1937).

title: Solidaridad Obrera publishes 'The Uselessness of Government'
summary: An article titled 'The Uselessness of Government' appeared in Solidaridad Obrera in the summer of 1936.

citation.quote: From Solidaridad Obrera, in the summer of 1936.

title: Liberal and socialist sector returned to power in elections
summary: The February 1936 elections hoisted the liberal and socialist sector back into power after two years of black reaction, though the bourgeois republicans' hesitancy was ultimately overruled by more extreme elements.

citation.chapter: THE SPANISH REVOLUTION (1936) IN RESPONSE TO FASCISM: A GENERAL STRIKE!
citation.quote: It goes without saying that the liberal and socialist sector, hoisted back into power by the February 1936 elections, after two years of black reaction, was greatly upset, but the hesitancy of the bourgeois republicans, who were more or less hungry for reforms, was in the last resort overruled by the audacity of more extreme elements.

title: Spanish libertarian communist congress at Zaragoza
summary: Spanish libertarian communists held a congress at Zaragoza expressing nostalgia for the 'free commune' and emphasizing affinity groups of nudists and naturists, on the eve of the social revolution.

citation.quote: Here there is a direct line of descent between Kropotkin and those Spanish libertarian communists who, at their congress ht Zaragoza in May 1936, were to wallow in nostalgia for a golden age, for the 'free commune" and support for the parochial focus upon the patria chica

title: CNT congress at Zaragoza
summary: The CNT held its congress at Zaragoza in May 1936, adopting a program that included utopian articles on the future revolution.

citation.quote: The reference is to certain utopian articles in the program adopted at CNT congress in Zaragoza in May 1936.

title: CNT third congress opens in Zaragoza
summary: The CNT's third congress, with about seven hundred delegates, opened in Zaragoza. Durruti, García Oliver and Francisco Ascaso were part of the Textile Union delegation.

citation.quote: The proceedings of the CNT's third congress, in Zaragoza, a congress in which about seven hundred delegates participated, opened on May 1, 1936.

title: Call for Moroccan autonomy at start of civil war
summary: Berneri argues that as early as July 1936, Morocco should have been formally declared politically autonomous to undermine Franco's operational base.

citation.chapter: The Contrary View-Open Letter to Federica Montseny
citation.quote: You are a member of a government which has offered France and England concessions in Morocco, whereas, as long ago as July 1936, Morocco ought to have been formally declared to be politically autonomous.

title: Workers seize factories and land in Spain
summary: Following the fascist uprising, Spanish workers and peasants took over factories and land as directors abandoned their posts, beginning a spontaneous experiment in collectivization and self-management.

citation.quote: On July 19 and the days that followed, every large undertaking was abandoned by its directors. The directors of the railway companies, urban transport companies, shipping lines, heavy steel industries, the textile industry, and the chairmen and representatives of the employers' associations had all vanished.

title: General strike halts Spanish economy for eight days
summary: The general strike unleashed by the working class to defend against the rebels brought the entire economic life of the country to a standstill for eight days.

citation.quote: The general strike which the working class had unleashed by way of defending itself against the rebels brought the entire economic life of the country to a standstill for eight days.

title: CNT unions take charge of production and supply
summary: After July 19, 1936, the CNT unions assumed control of production and supply across Spain, setting up canteens on union premises and distributing provisions via supply committees backed by union-guaranteed vouchers.

citation.quote: After 19 July 1936, the CNT unions took charge of production and supply. At first, the unions strove to resolve the most pressing problem: keeping the population supplied. In every district, canteens were set up on the union premises.

title: Workers take over firms following the July Revolution
summary: Following the Revolution of July 19, workers in Catalonia took over their firms and elected workers' councils, introducing self-management in anticipation of any legislation.

citation.quote: Reproduced below, virtually in its entirety, is the Decree of Collectivization of Catalonia's industries which, as we would say today, institutionalized se fl-management which had been introduced, in anticipation of any legislation, by the workers themselves when, following the Revolution of July 19, they had taken over their firms and elected workers' councils.

title: CNT calls general strike against fascist military revolt
summary: The CNT Regional Committee of Catalonia issued a manifesto calling for a general strike in response to the fascist military uprising, warning that fascism had taken Seville and North Africa and a revolt had occurred in Cordoba.

citation.chapter: THE SPANISH REVOLUTION (1936) IN RESPONSE TO FASCISM: A GENERAL STRIKE!

title: Army revolt against the Spanish Republic
summary: The army revolt of July 19, 1936 had profound implications for Spain's economic life. The struggle against the clerico-militarist clan was only possible through the help of the working class, as the republican bourgeoisie would otherwise have been overwhelmed.

citation.chapter: THE SPANISH REVOLUTION (1936) IN RESPONSE TO FASCISM: A GENERAL STRIKE!
citation.quote: The army revolt of July 19, 1936 has had profound implications for Spain's economic life. The struggle against the clerico-militarist clan was rendered possible only through the help of the working class.

title: Beginning of a new era proclaimed by FAI
summary: The FAI manifesto declared July 19 as marking the beginning of a new era, referring to the antifascist uprising in Barcelona that initiated the Spanish revolution.

citation.quote: July 19 marks the beginning of a new era: the peace of the past is no more.

title: Rebel troops defeated in Barcelona
summary: Rebel troops took to the streets of Barcelona at 5:00 A.M. on July 19, and by 5:00 P.M. García Oliver reported over Radio Barcelona that the people had beaten the fascists. The CNT and FAI became masters of Barcelona.

citation.quote: Rebel troops took to the streets of Barcelona at 5:00 A.M. On July 19, and at 5:00 P.M., on the Monday afternoon, Garcia Oliver reported over Radio Barcelona that the people had beaten the fascists in the course of an unequal battle.

title: Disintegration of the Spanish army
summary: The CNT proclamation noted that the old Spanish army vanished as of July 19, 1936, the day of the military uprising and popular resistance, arguing the bourgeois republic should not rebuild it.

citation.quote: The Spanish army, which vanished as of July 19, for all the rigidity of its military code, was not at all outstanding for its discipline, its courage nor its organization.

title: Anarchists and trade unionists confront fascist generals
summary: On July 19, 1936, the anarchists and trade unionists led the revolutionary movement against the fascist generals' uprising, going on to create the antifascist militias and collectivize industry in Catalonia, primarily through CNT-FAI initiative.

citation.chapter: THE USELESSNESS OF GOVERNMENT (A MANIFESTO ADOPTED BY THE CNT)
citation.quote: On July 19, it was the anarchists and trade unionists who marched at the head of the revolutionary movement to confront the fascist generals. The creation of antifascist militias and the collectivization of industry in Catalonia were primarily the handiwork of the CNT-FAI.

title: Spanish Revolution begins on July 19
summary: Montseny refers to the social Revolution begun by the majority of the people on July 19, arguing that had the war been won, nothing would have prevented its expansion and completion.

citation.chapter: FEDERICA MONTSENY SETS THE RECORD STRAIGHT
citation.quote: Nothing and nobody would have prevented the expansion and completion of what the majority of the people had begun on July 19.

title: Garcia Oliver fights on the Barcelona barricades
summary: Juan Garcia Oliver, a leader of the FAI, fought on the barricades on July 19, 1936, at the start of the Spanish Civil War in Barcelona.

citation.quote: Juan Garcia Oliver (1897–1980), one of the activist leaders of the Iberian Anarchist Federation (FAI): from 1923, he served a prison sentence from which the revolution of 1931 and an amnesty released him: fought on the barricades on July 19, 1936

title: Ascaso killed at Atarazanas barracks
summary: Libertarian activist Francisco Ascaso Abadia, friend and companion of Durruti, was killed in the storming of the Atarazanas barracks in Barcelona on July 20, 1936.

citation.quote: Francisco Ascaso Abadia (1900–1936), libertarian activist, friend and indefatigable companion of Durruti, killed in the storming of the Atarazanas barracks on July 20, 1936.

title: Durruti column sets out for Aragon
summary: The Durruti-Farras column set out from Barcelona for Lerida with fewer men than expected, heading toward Caspe and Bujaraloz, where it dug in some 30 km from Zaragoza.

citation.quote: On July 23, the column set out for Lerida with fewer men than had been expected, in that it had been reckoning on 10,000 men to start with.

title: FAI Peninsular Committee broadcasts manifesto over radio
summary: The Iberian Anarchist Federation's Peninsular Committee broadcast a manifesto over the radio addressing the people of Barcelona, calling for continued resistance against fascism and celebrating the antifascist column advancing on Zaragoza.

citation.quote: On July 26, the FAI Peninsular Committee broadcast this manifesto over the radio:

title: Libertarian communism introduced in Lecera
summary: Manuel Martinez took up office as social sub-delegate in Lecera, introducing the libertarian communist system and abolishing money in the village.

citation.quote: — Nearly three months. On August 25, he took up office, introducing the libertarian communist system since then and doing away with money in the village.

title: Durruti meets Largo Caballero in Madrid
summary: Around mid-September, Durruti went to Madrid for talks with the socialist prime minister and minister of War Largo Caballero, who promised a loan of 1800 million pesetas for arms and Catalan war industries.

citation.quote: Around mid-September, Durruti went to Madrid for talks with the socialist Largo Caballero' who was simultaneously prime minister and minister of War, and who assured him of a loan of 1800 million pesetas for the purchase of arms and the running of the Catalan war industries.

title: CNT reverses stance and petitions for National Defense Council
summary: Within weeks of the manifesto rejecting government participation, the CNT reversed course and petitioned Prime Minister Largo Caballero to establish a fifteen-member National Defense Council with five seats reserved for the CNT, a step toward cabinet membership.

citation.chapter: THE USELESSNESS OF GOVERNMENT (A MANIFESTO ADOPTED BY THE CNT)
citation.quote: However, within a few weeks, in mid-September 1936, the CNT reversed its stance. In the name of "antifascist unity," it saw fit to petition the Spanish prime minister, Largo Caballero, for the establishment of a fifteen-member "National Defense Council," in which five places would be reserved for it.

title: Largo Caballero serves as premier
summary: Francisco Largo Caballero served as premier and minister of War of the Spanish republic from September 5, 1936 to May 15, 1937.

citation.quote: Francisco Largo Caballero (1869–1946), of worker extraction, reformist socialist, secretary of the General Workers' Union (UGT): radicalized during the Asturias strike in 1934: premier and minister of War from September 5, 1936 to May 15, 1937

title: Decree on Collectivization of the Catalan Economy
summary: The Generalidad of Catalonia issued the Decree of Collectivization, the first legislative document since the Russian Revolution of 1917 to define how workers' power and workers' control might be exercised democratically.

citation.quote: The Decree of October 24, 1936, and particularly this last-mentioned provision, have been quite perceptively glossed by certain anarchist authors like Vernon Richards in his Lessons of the Spanish Revolution (1953).

title: Berneri writes on Moroccan autonomy in Guerra di classe
summary: Berneri publishes an article in Guerra di classe arguing for stepped-up propaganda in favor of Moroccan autonomy throughout the pan-Islamic sphere to undermine Franco's base.

citation.chapter: The Contrary View-Open Letter to Federica Montseny
citation.quote: On October 24, 1936, I wrote in *Guerra dt* classe: "The fascist army's op­erational base is Morocco. Propaganda in favor of Moroccan autonomy must be stepped up throughout the wholepan-Islamic sphere ofinfluence."

title: Italian Section of Ascaso Column opposes militarization at Monte Pelado
summary: Volunteers of the Ascaso Column's Italian Section, stationed at Monte Pelado, issue a statement rejecting the Generalidad Council's decree to militarize the militias, declaring they would consider themselves released from any moral obligation if forced to comply.

citation.chapter: THE ITALIAN SECTION OF THE ASCASO COLUMN OPPOSES MILITARIZATION
citation.quote: **(MONTE PELADO, OCTOBER 30, 1936)**

title: Defense of Madrid against Nationalist assault
summary: After the Republican government's departure for Valencia, the Madrid Defense Committee organized resistance to the fascist advance on the capital, with CNT mobilization and Durruti's column joining the defense.

citation.quote: **(NOVEMBER-DECEMBER 1936)**

title: Durruti arrives in Madrid with Catalan fighters
summary: Buenaventura Durruti arrived in Madrid with five thousand Catalan fighters, issuing a radio proclamation offering every Madrileño a rifle or a pick and calling on all to dig trenches and throw up barricades.

citation.quote: The arrival of Durruti with five thousand Catalan fighters; the rough, manly proclamation he issued over the airwaves, giving a good tongue-lashing to the idlers, poseurs and phony revolutionaries; the offer he made to give every MADRILENQ a rifle or a pick, and the invitation to all to dig trenches and throw up barricades–all of it helped create a sort of enthusiastic, joyous euphoria

title: CNT mobilizes 40,000 workers for Madrid's defense
summary: The Local Federation of the Sindicatos Unicos of Madrid mobilized all workers under its control, declaring all non-war works suspended and placing forty thousand confederated workers under arms to defend the capital.

citation.quote: The Local Federation of the Sindicatos Unicos of Madrid, whose responsibility is bound up with the fate of the antifascist cause, yesterday, Monday, mobilized all of the workers under its control in order to make a decisive contribution to the fight against the rebels on the outskirts of the Republic's capital. All works not bearing directly upon the war have been declared suspended, and today there are forty thousand confederated workers under arms in Madrid to bolster the government.

title: CNT proclamation on revolutionary discipline
summary: A CNT proclamation dated November argued that revolutionary discipline grows from conscious duty rather than constraint, rejecting the rigid military codes of the old bourgeois army for the people's militias.

citation.quote: Their propaganda, inspired by a preoccupation with consolidating the militias' gains within the frameworks of the people's army, took a freer, more revolutionary turn. Thus, one proclamation dated November stated:

title: Durruti arrives in Madrid with his column
summary: When Madrid came under Francoist attack in October–November 1936, the government summoned Durruti's column. Durruti arrived on November 12 and was assigned to the most dangerous sector.

citation.quote: And so, to the delight of the capital's inhabitants, Durruti arrived on November 12 at the head of his men, and without so much as being given time to rest up, was assigned to the most dangerous sector.

title: Iron Column delegate addresses Regional Plenum in Valencia
summary: An Iron Column delegate's address to the Regional Plenum in Valencia is endorsed by the column and reprinted in its mouthpiece Linea de Fuego on the Teruel front, opposing militarization and single command of the CNT militias.

citation.chapter: THE ITALIAN SECTION OF THE ASCASO COLUMN OPPOSES MILITARIZATION
citation.quote: AN IRON COLUMN DELEGATE'S ADDRESS TO THE REGIONAL PLENUM IN VALENCIA (ENDORSED BY THE COLUMN AND REPRINTED IN ITS MOUTHPIECE LINEA DE FUEGO [TERUEL FRONT] ON NOVEMBER I7, 1936)

title: Durruti shot at the Clinical Hospital, Madrid
summary: Around 2:00 p.m. on November 19, Durruti was hit in the lung by a 'stray bullet' while facing the Clinical Hospital overlooking University City, and rushed to the Catalan militias' hospital in the Ritz Hotel.

citation.quote: Around 2:00 p.m. on November 19th, Durruti was hit right in the lung by a "stray bullet" while facing the Clinical Hospital, a stronghold overlooking the University City, where the fascists were dug in.

title: Death of Durruti
summary: After several operations at the Catalan militias' hospital in the Ritz Hotel, Durruti died at 6:00 A.M. on November 20, 1936.

citation.quote: There he underwent several operations, before dying at 6:00 A.M. the next day, November 20.

title: Hundreds of thousands attend Durruti's funeral
summary: Hundreds of thousands of people paid their final tribute to the anarchist militia leader Buenaventura Durruti, who had been killed fighting fascist forces in the streets of Madrid.

citation.quote: And now Durruti is dead. His heart beats no more. His imposing physique cut down like some giant tree. Yet Durruti is not dead. The hundreds of thousands who paid their final tribute to Durruti on November 22, 1936 bear witness to that.

title: Durruti's funeral in Barcelona
summary: Durruti's funeral in the Catalan capital was attended by upwards of half a million people, after his body was covertly removed from Madrid.

citation.quote: His funeral in the Catalan capital on November 23 was attended by upwards of a half million people.

title: Pravda announces purge of Catalonian anarchists and Trotskyists
summary: Pravda publishes a plan announcing that the purging of Trotskyist and anarchist syndicalist elements in Catalonia has begun and will be prosecuted with the same vigor as in the USSR.

citation.chapter: The Contrary View-Open Letter to Federica Montseny
citation.quote: The masses must be called upon to judge whether certain ploys designed to sabotage supplies are not part and parcel of the plan announced on December 17, 1936 by *Pravda:* "As for Catalonia, the purging of Trotskyist and anarchist syndicalist elements has begun; this endeavor will be prosecuted with the same vigor with which it has been carried out in the USSR."

title: Berneri, Goldman, and Faure raise the CNT government issue
summary: Camillo Berneri, Emma Goldman and Sebastien Faure publicly broached the question of CNT participation in government during the Spanish war and Revolution, while Rudolf Rocker and Max Nettlau refrained from judgment.

citation.chapter: FEDERICA MONTSENY SETS THE RECORD STRAIGHT
citation.quote: Back in 1937, Camillo Berneri, Emma Goldman and Sebastien Faure broached this matter. Others, like Rudolf Rocker and Max Nettlau refrained from judgment and trusted us.

title: Prudhommeaux publishes Catalogne 36–37
summary: Andre Prudhommeaux's Catalogne 36–37 was published in 1937, drawing on his work in Cahiers de terre libre.

citation.quote: Text taken from Andre Prudhommeaux's Cahiers de terre libre and his Catalogne 36–37 (1937)

title: Montseny's Barcelona lecture on Pi y Margall
summary: In a January 1937 public lecture in Barcelona, Federica Montseny praised the regionalism of Francisco Pi y Margall, drawing criticism from Gaston Leval and Berneri.

citation.quote: In January 1937, in a public lecture in Barcelona, Federica Montseny sang the praises of the regionalism of Francisco Pi y Margall (1821–1901), a disciple of Proudhon.

title: Montseny's speech defending anarchist entry into government
summary: Federica Montseny delivered a speech declaring anarchists had entered the government to prevent deviation in the Revolution, prosecute it beyond the war, and oppose dictatorial ambitions.

citation.chapter: The Contrary View-Open Letter to Federica Montseny
citation.quote: In your speech of January 3 \[1937\], you said: "Anarchists have entered the

title: CNT quits the Caballero government after May events in Barcelona
summary: Federica Montseny and her CNT colleagues left the Largo Caballero government after the May 1937 events in Barcelona, which she describes as a coup contrived by Russian agents to stamp out the anarchist movement in Spain.

citation.quote: On the day when we quit the Caballero government, after the May 1937 events in Barcelona–a coup carefully contrived by Russian agents casting around for an excuse to stamp out the anarchist movement in Spain–I was immensely relieved, as I imagine my colleagues were too.
